name: Methylmercury
aliases: methylmercury, methyl mercury, MeHg, mercury, metilmercurio
what_is: Methylmercury is a form of mercury that builds up through aquatic food chains. Fish absorb it from what they eat, so large, long-lived predators can contain much more than smaller species.
why_botia: Methylmercury binds to proteins in the body and reaches the nervous system, where it can damage coordination, vision and sensation; the developing brain is the most vulnerable. It crosses the placenta: cord blood can contain higher concentrations than maternal blood, and methylmercury also passes into breast milk. In the food chain it builds up most in large, long-lived predators — swordfish, shark and large tuna — so the practical message is not to stop eating fish, but to choose lower-mercury species. JECFA set a provisional tolerable weekly intake of 1.6 µg/kg body weight for methylmercury to protect the developing nervous system.
can_1: Explain why large, long-lived predatory fish tend to contain more methylmercury than smaller species.
can_2: Explain why the Woman layer matters: methylmercury crosses the placenta, cord blood can contain more than maternal blood, and exposure can continue through breast milk.
